title: The TDR offer-suggestion slice in rwb-agent: the operation path below the base, the treatment and account read operations, the parameter keys, the screen route, the run version fields, the inputs reference and the two waits of the call are not fixed by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-032 sections 3, 4, 12, 13 and 16; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.10 (FEAT-AGT-10) and A2.1 (BR-P10-010, VR-P10-010-1); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-111), T3.2, T5.1, T6 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 8, 16, 41, 42, 43 and the call matrix; Ownership Map v1 (agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_run owner P10; GET /admin/agent-runs and GET /admin/agent-configs owner P10; EV-28 owner P10; AgentRunWorkflow owner P10); Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC9 to AC15; 9 State transitions; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.8; 13; 15 Screens and states
description: Seven values the rwb-agent slice of this key needs are absent or unresolved in the sources. (1) The legacy in-process interface ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer becomes one REST operation, and no source gives its path below the base /api/recovery/agent/v1, its request media type or its refusal codes beyond the legacy DecisionNotRecordedException and MSG-P10-007. (2) The legacy story reads the account balance, the arrears and the payments 'through the P3 interface', and no rwb-source-data operation or data product returns v_ace_account and v_ace_payment fields, so the read path is open while DP-05 forbids the direct table read. (3) The treatment and its type are read from treatment.treatment_type in the legacy monolith, and in the target they belong either to the runtime owner rwb-treatment (S2, Arch v5 slide 41) or to the contract baseline RWB-P3-E2004-CON that the split plan puts in the C list, and no source says which operation answers at run time. (4) The parameter keys the story reads and the reference-data operation for LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY and LOV-AGENT-RUN are not named, and the feature flag rwb.agent.tdr-suggestion of the legacy section 13 has no home beyond the §R3 default ruling that feature flags are a platform library. (5) The suggestion area of SCR-14 and the gateway-bff route in front of the two admin reads have no name, path, field order or masking rule. (6) agent_run requires agent_version (DF-AGT-038, required) while the legacy decision-log mapping fixes agent_version null, and no source gives the agent_version or the prompt_version of the TDR model, or the type and length of the inputs reference of the record. (7) Two waits conflict: the legacy operation answers with the suggestion after a model call of up to 60 seconds, while DP-11 fixes one hop with a 2 s client budget for a published interface, and no source reconciles the suggestion call with that budget. The story keeps the legacy behaviour and settles each value as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-032 section 3 ('reads the account balance, arrears and the last 12 months of payments through the P3 interface and masks personal fields'), section 12 (the published interface, the decision log mapping and the two admin paths), section 13 ('Package', 'Database: no new table', 'Feature flag: rwb.agent.tdr-suggestion'), section 4 step 2 (P3 treatment service calls ModelSuggestionClient) and section 11 (DF-TRT-004 treatment.treatment_type, DF-ACC-009, DF-ACE-018, DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-025, DF-ACE-045, DF-ACE-046); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-038 agent_version NOT NULL, DF-AGT-039 prompt_version, DF-AGT-058 decision_log_id) and T-A.1 (eleven P10 operations, none of them a suggestion); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-agent IN: GET /agent-runs/{id}, GET/POST /agent-policies; OUT: Enterprise AI endpoint) and slide 41 (rwb-treatment owns treatments); Template and Rules v1 §R3 default ruling (parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case, feature flags to the platform library) and §R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-11, DP-13 and DP-19
area: Agent runtime / model gateway call, contract and screen composition
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 service owner and the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and rwb-decision
proposed: Keep the legacy behaviour and the legacy values; give the operation a place under the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 fixed in RWB-P10-E2032-CON; read the account and the payments through rwb-source-data and the treatment through rwb-treatment with the RWB-P3-E2004-CON baseline; read the parameters and the lists through the rwb-case contracts; treat the suggestion call as the recorded exception of DP-11 that carries the 60-second policy timeout while every other hop keeps 2 s; record agent_version null as the legacy mapping requires; and compose SCR-14 and the admin reads through the gateway-bff route. Every value is settled in the assumption rows cited and no literal is invented.

title: The TDR offer-suggestion contract slice: the operation path and request members, the record member types, the boundary answer and error mapping, the admin read route and the two-wait exception are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-032 section 12 (published interface, decision log mapping, external call, the two admin paths); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.10 and A2.1; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (P10 API rows, EV-28, agent tables); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.3; 12.5; 13; 19 Out of scope
description: Five elements of the contract slice are open in the sources. (1) The operation that replaces ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer has no published path, no declared request body beyond the case ID and the treatment ID, and no refusal code set; the legacy interface declares only the exception and the two messages. (2) The decision-record payload mapping of the legacy section 12 names case_id, decision_code D5, model_version, agent_version null, inputs_ref, recommendation, final_call and the actions, but no source gives the type, the length or the member names of inputs_ref or of recommendation, and agent_run.agent_version is required while the mapping fixes it null. (3) The EV-28 payload is named by Arch v5 slide 43 and by TSD P10 v2 T5.3 without a member list, so the payload members of this key are taken from the agent_run fields of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 and not from any published schema. (4) The model gateway answer at the INT-23 boundary is described only as an answer checked against the output schema tdr-offer-v1; no source gives the answer shape, the error taxonomy or the mapping of a 4xx and a 5xx to a status of LOV-AGENT-RUN. (5) The gateway-bff route in front of the two admin reads has no name or path, and the 60-second suggestion call sits against the 2 s client budget of DP-11 with no source reconciling the two.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-032 section 12 (the Java interface and the OfferSuggestion record; the decision log mapping; 'External call: INT-23 through ModelGatewayClient; request: model code, masked inputs, output schema tdr-offer-v1; per request'; GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs and GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-038 required, DF-AGT-049 output, DF-AGT-058 decision_log_id), T3.2 (LOV-AGENT-RUN) and T5.1 (INT-23, per request); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43 row 28 (AgentRunCompleted on rwb.agent.events.v1, consumers rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-deviation) and the slide 42 note (CloudEvents, key caseId, no personal data); Template and Rules v1 §R4 (event name pattern) and §R5.5 DP-03, DP-09, DP-11 and DP-19
area: Contract: agent operation, decision record, event payload and model boundary
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect and the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and rwb-source-data
proposed: Fix the operation under the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 with the three request members and the eight legacy answer members; keep the legacy record mapping member for member and let the member types be agreed with the record owner; declare the EV-28 payload from the agent_run fields of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 with the case ID as key; fix the boundary request to the model code, the masked inputs and tdr-offer-v1 and map a timeout, a 4xx, a 5xx and a schema failure to TIMED_OUT, MODEL_ERROR and GUARDRAIL_FAILED; declare the admin reads as restated from RWB-P10-E1058-CON and the route as a pass-through. The app story and its tests build against these shapes and the fakes.

title: The infrastructure slice of the TDR offer-suggestion key: the INT-23 host, port, certificate and Key Vault names, the partition and retention values, the sizing, the budget measurement points and the alarm thresholds are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-032 sections 3, 12 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.10; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T5.1, T5.3, T6.2 and T7 (NFR-010); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 8, 16, 35, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11; Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC7; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: Six environment values of this key are absent from every source. (1) The Enterprise AI private endpoint INT-23 has no host, port, certificate subject or certificate authority named; only the approach 'private endpoint in the SCB tenant' and the direction 'Both, per request' are given. (2) The Key Vault entries of the model gateway call have no names, and the rwb-agent service login has no name although DP-02 requires one login per service. (3) The topic rwb.agent.events.v1 has no partition count, replication factor, retention or retry policy, and the retry and .dlt topic names follow the §R4 pattern but are not written in any source. (4) The Temporal worker concurrency, poller count, activity timeouts and the queue's rate limits are not given, and no source states the rwb-agent worker identity. (5) The 60-second model budget and the 2 s client budget are stated as targets (NFR-010, ADR-020) with no measurement point, no percentile and no alarm threshold. (6) The capacity of the pods, the scaling rule for a burst of runs and the four operator alarms have no figures. No source names a Blob container for agent artefacts either: the policies, the prompts and the samples are rows of agent_policy, agent_prompt and agent_sample in rwb_agent, so no container is created and none is invented.
evidence: TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T5.1 ('INT-23 | Enterprise AI model endpoint | Both | Private endpoint in the SCB tenant | Per request') and T7 (NFR-010 'An agent returns an answer within its target, after which the rule result is used and the case still routes | Under 60 seconds'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-agent OUT: Enterprise AI endpoint, HTTPS private endpoint), slide 35 ('rwb-agent: 60 s, or the rule result is used'), slide 41 (schema, topic, task queue and wave per service) and slide 43 row 28 (AgentRunCompleted); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11 (namespace rwb-recovery, one task queue per service, KEDA scales workers on backlog); Template and Rules v1 §R4 (topic, retry and .dlt pattern, task queue and login per service) and DP-02, DP-09 and DP-11
area: Infrastructure: private endpoint, identity and secrets, topic, queue, NFR budgets, capacity and gates
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the ACE platform team and security
proposed: Provision the private path to INT-23 with TLS and mTLS, the login and the Key Vault entries, the topic with its retry and .dlt topics and the producer ACL, the queue and the worker identity, the two measured budgets with their alarms, the sizing and the five pipeline gates, and record every environment value as a reviewed value per environment rather than a template constant. No table, no bucket and no business value is created.

title: The decision scope of a version, the autonomy value set, the right of the change, the record rule version, the load file and the approval instant are not fixed by any source
source: RWB-E3-030 sections 1 to 16; FSD P10 v3 A2.12 (FEAT-AGT-12), A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-02 and AC-EXC-P10-001-03, A2.5 and A2.6; TSD P10 v2 T3.0, T3.1 (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-043), T3.2, T6.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P10-001 to API-P10-004); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 16, 35 and 41 to 44; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 rows E3 P10 FEAT-AGT-12 and P3 FEAT-CWC-22; Ownership Map v1 (agent_policy and agent_prompt owner P10, decision_log_entry and rule_row owner P7, parameter_catalog and parameter_value owner P3, the three admin config operations owner P10); Template and Rules v1 §R3 default rulings and §R5.5
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC3 to AC9; 8 Business rules; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: Seven values this slice needs are absent or unresolved in the sources. (1) The legacy criterion changes a level for one agent AND one decision, but agent_policy has no decision column: it holds agent_code, policy_version, autonomy_mode and the two segment columns, so the unit of change is a version of the agent and the per-decision key has no home in this table. (2) The autonomy value set is split across sources: TSD P10 v2 T3.2 lists LOV-AUTONOMY as OFF, SHADOW and L1, RWB-AD-020 uses L1 and L2, and the legacy screen names the states Shadow, live and paused, so which values a change may set and how a state maps to a value is not stated anywhere. (3) The right of the change conflicts: the legacy permission check gives Platform administration R to six roles and never names the risk and model risk officer as an actor, while TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 governs the three configuration operations by Rules and parameters with rights R, C and A and FSD P10 v3 A2.12.3.3 names the risk and model risk officer as primary. (4) The legacy criterion writes the result to the decision log WITH THE RULE VERSION, but no Drools package decides a configuration change and rule_row stays with rwb-decision, so the version that belongs on the record must be named. (5) The load is described as a checked file whose columns, order and format no source gives. (6) The approval needs an instant and an approver role, while agent_policy carries approved_by and no approved_at, and the role of an approver is a row of rwb-access and not of this table. (7) The flyway number of any migration, if the baseline does not carry the tables, and the name of the per-service login are not in any source. The legacy story also carries no requirement ID and no BRD in the extracts carries FEAT-AGT-12, so section 18 traces the feature and no requirement.
evidence: FSD P10 v3 A2.12.4.1 gives one criterion with the words 'The data and rules it needs are in place', 'The user acts' and 'The result is recorded with its rule version', and BR-P10-012 only forbids a value in code; TSD P10 v2 T3.1 lists agent_policy with no decision column, approved_at missing and review_date optional, and T3.2 lists LOV-AUTONOMY as OFF, SHADOW and L1 with LOV-CONFIG-STATUS LOADED, APPROVED and RETIRED; TSD T6.1 gives a Platform administration matrix only and no Rules and parameters matrix, while T-A.1 assigns the three config operations to Rules and parameters C, A and R; FSD A2.1 AC-ALT-P10-001-01 shows a prompt version loaded, approved with a valid-from date and applied per date, AC-EXC-P10-001-02 shows a failed check refused with 422 and a named check, and AC-EXC-P10-001-03 shows the loader refused when approving their own version with 409; the legacy story RWB-E3-030 names the screen SCR-46 with the states Shadow, live and paused and the endpoint GET /admin/agent-runs under Platform administration R; Architecture v5 slide 16 names GET/POST /agent-policies (admin) as the service summary and slide 41 puts agent policies and prompts in schema rwb_agent; the Ownership Map names the three config operations and the tables under P10 and parameter_catalog, parameter_value and rule_row elsewhere.
area: Agent runtime / autonomy configuration and decision record
owner_role: Solution architect with the service owner of rwb-agent and the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-case
proposed: Hold the level as autonomy_mode of the policy version and accept only the values of LOV-AUTONOMY (OFF, SHADOW, L1), leaving L2 to the step-up key RWB-P10-E8004; carry the per-decision key in RWB-P10-AD020-APP and keep the version as the unit of change here; read the change as Rules and parameters C and A with the legacy row as the read on the monitor; name the configuration version in the rule-version element of the record; fix the file column set from the FSD field catalog and TSD T3.1 at the wave 2 contract freeze; take the approval instant from updated_at and the approver role from rwb-access; confirm the migration number with the DB story and the login with the platform naming.

title: The operation path of a configuration change, the record payload members, the approval instant, the kind value set and the state mapping are not fixed by one source
source: RWB-E3-030 sections 1 to 16; FSD P10 v3 A2.12, A2.1 AC-ALT-P10-001-01 and AC-EXC-P10-001-02 to AC-EXC-P10-001-03; TSD P10 v2 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P10-002 to API-P10-004); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 10, 13, 16, 20 and 41; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 16; Ownership Map v1 (the three admin config operations owner P10, decision_log_entry owner P7, role and permission owner P4, parameter_catalog, parameter_value, reference_row and lov_value owner P3); RWB-AD-020 AC1 and AC2; Template and Rules v1 §R3 and §R5.5
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: Four disagreements and three absences bear on this contract. (1) The path of a configuration change is named twice, differently: the service summary of Arch v5 slide 16 carries GET/POST /agent-policies (admin), while the operation inventory of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 and the Ownership Map carry GET and POST /admin/agent-configs and POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve, and R-PREC puts the Arch slides first, so the contract must say which reading it fixes. (2) The record payload has a shape but no member names: the Temporal and Drools design slide 16 lists chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash and entry_hash while the configuration element that must travel on a change is named by no source. (3) The kind of a version is a query parameter and a multipart field in TSD T-A.2, and T3.2 carries no list for it, so the value set POLICY and PROMPT is inferred from the two resource names agent_policy and agent_prompt. (4) agent_policy carries approved_by and no approved_at, so an approval instant is an element no column supplies. (5) The autonomy value set is split between LOV-AUTONOMY (OFF, SHADOW, L1), RWB-AD-020 (L1 and L2) and the legacy screen states (Shadow, live, paused). (6) The column set and order of the loaded file are not in any source, and the wording of MSG-P7-002 and MSG-P10-001 is not in the legacy message set or the extracts. (7) The login that serves the three operations is not named by any source.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 16 IN line reads REST GET /agent-runs/{id}; GET/POST /agent-policies (admin) and slide 41 puts the policies and prompts in schema rwb_agent with the base /api/recovery/agent/v1; TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 names API-P10-002 GET /admin/agent-configs, API-P10-003 POST /admin/agent-configs and API-P10-004 POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve with Rules and parameters R, C and A and the Idempotency-Key header on the two writes, and T-A.2 gives their errors 401, 403, 409, 422, 503 and 401, 403, 404, 409, 503; TSD T3.1 gives agent_policy DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025 with approved_by and no approved_at and T3.0 gives updated_at as a standard column; T3.2 gives LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-AGENT and no kind list; the Temporal and Drools design slide 11 states that the service writes its state change, the decision record and the outbox row in one transaction and slide 16 lists the record fields; RWB-AD-020 AC2 speaks of a committee approval for L2 and the legacy story RWB-E3-030 names the screen states Shadow, live and paused; the Ownership Map names the three operations and the tables under P10 and role, permission, parameter_catalog and lov_value elsewhere; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row E3 P10 FEAT-AGT-12 carries no requirement ID.
area: Agent runtime / configuration contract and record contract
owner_role: Solution architect with the service owner of rwb-agent and the owners of rwb-decision and rwb-access
proposed: Fix the three /admin/agent-configs operations as the contract and record the Arch v5 summary label as a summary; name the configuration version in the rule-version element of the record and leave the library's JSON member names to RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; fix the kind value set as POLICY and PROMPT from the two resource names; take the approval instant from updated_at and the approver role from rwb-access; accept only the values of LOV-AUTONOMY and leave L2 and the state mapping to the step-up and monitor keys; settle the file column set and the two message texts at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: RWB-AD-020 in rwb-agent: the step scope of a policy version, the L2 value, the approval reference column, the take-effect rule, the route agent code, the P1 fact read, the response field names, the record members, the no-version case, the login and the requirement row are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-020); WP B-P10-03; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.12, A2.15 and Screens; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1, T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 35, 41, 50; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 16; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (decision_log_entry and the LOV-DECISION row); Ownership Map v1
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC3 to AC11; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1, 12.2, 12.5, 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: The legacy story names the behaviour of the per-step autonomy level but none of the values the rwb-agent slice needs. (1) No column of agent_policy names a decision step: DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025 carry agent_code, policy_version, autonomy_mode, valid_from, valid_to and status, and a jsonb promotion_conditions, so a version cannot say which step it governs without an assumption. (2) LOV-AUTONOMY lists OFF, SHADOW and L1 only (TSD P10 v2 T3.2), while legacy AC2 names L2; no source defines the ladder or the position of L2 in it. (3) agent_policy carries approved_by (DF-AGT-025) and no approval reference column, while legacy AC2 requires the version to show the approval reference. (4) No source states when a version is 'in force': status, valid_from and valid_to exist, and no text defines the reading or what happens when two versions cover one date. (5) The route agent that answers at step D6.3 has no value of LOV-AGENT, whose five values are INTAKE, SCREENING, LEGAL_DOC, EXTRACT and TDR_OFFER. (6) The rwb-source-data operation that returns the case facts a step answers on is not named; Architecture v5 slide 15 lists only the customer, account, collateral, payment, freshness and business-day operations. (7) The field names of the three read resources (AgentRun, AgentConfigVersion, AgentOutput) do not exist in any source, and the gateway-bff route of SCR-46 has no name or path. (8) The decision record has no field for the autonomy mode or the policy version, and its approval_level (DF-DEC-011) is the delegation ladder L1 to L6 of LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, whose L1 collides with the autonomy L1. (9) No source states what a step does when no version is in force. (10) The per-service login name and the Flyway file number of any later migration are not given. (11) The legacy story carries no requirement ID and no BRD in the extracts carries FEAT-AGT-12 or FEAT-AGT-15.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-020 (story line, AC1, AC2, Data table naming decision_log_entry and DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, endpoint table naming the monolith admin base, screen SCR-46 with states Shadow, live and paused); TSD P10 v2 T3.1 DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025 (no step column), DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060 (no step column, autonomy_mode DF-AGT-043, decision_log_id DF-AGT-058), T3.2 LOV-AUTONOMY = OFF, SHADOW, L1; T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P10-001, API-P10-002 and API-P10-010 with response types and no field lists; FSD P10 v3 A2.12 'for one agent and one decision, as a versioned configuration row' and A2.15; Logical Data Model v8 DF-DEC-003 (decision_code, LOV-DECISION 'D1 to D9 with sub-decisions, X1 to X7'), DF-DEC-011 approval_level, DF-DEC-038 approval_level L1 to L6; Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 rwb-valuation owns the D6 route decision and the route agent output); Ownership Map v1 (agent tables P10, decision_log_entry and approval P7, POST /authorise P4, GET /approvals/{approvalId} P7)
proposed: Keep the legacy behaviour and settle each value as an assumption: the step is a named member of promotion_conditions until a decision_code column is agreed; L2 is the next level above L1 named by the criteria and is added to LOV-AUTONOMY by its owner; the approval reference is a named member of the same jsonb; a version is in force when its status is APPROVED and the run date is inside its window, with one version per step and date; the run is identified by its step and not by an agent code; the case facts come through rwb-source-data's contract; the three read resources gain step, autonomyMode, policyVersion and approvalRef; the record carries decision_code plus the members autonomyMode and policyVersion of recommendation and never uses approval_level; a step with no version in force resolves OFF; the login is 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)' and no migration number is claimed; no requirement ID is cited and the feature is traced instead.

title: The per-step autonomy contract slice: the four element names, the record member names, the recommendation marker, the route-output operation, the contract artefact names and the types are not specified by any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-020); WP B-P10-03; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.12 and A2.15; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2 (API-P10-001, API-P10-002, API-P10-010); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 16; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; Ownership Map v1
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC7; 8 Business rules; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.2, 12.7, 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: The contract slice has to fix names that no source gives. (1) The three read resources are typed as AgentRun, AgentConfigVersion and AgentOutput in TSD P10 v2 T-A.2 with no field list, so the four elements this contract adds - the step, the autonomy mode, the policy version label and the approval reference - have no published name, type or length. (2) The decision record has no field for the autonomy mode or the policy version, and its approval_level is the delegation ladder L1 to L6, so the two members of recommendation and their keys are a choice of this contract. (3) No source names an element that marks an answer as a recommendation at L1, and the collision with an applied outcome has to be resolved without a business value in code. (4) The operation that returns rwb-valuation's route agent output for the route decision D6 is not named: the Ownership Map names only POST /cases/{caseId}/route, which starts the route decision and does not return the agent output. (5) The contract file names, their formats and the split between the four artefacts are this story's choice. (6) LOV-DECISION is given as a range, so the sub-decision D6.3 of the legacy criterion is named only by the legacy story and the contract cites it as a value without listing the range. (7) The legacy story carries no requirement ID, so no BRD section is cited for the slice.
evidence: TSD P10 v2 T-A.2 (API-P10-001 Response AgentRun[], API-P10-002 Response AgentConfigVersion[], API-P10-010 Response AgentOutput[], no field lists) and T3.1 (no step column, no autonomy field on the record); Logical Data Model v8 DF-DEC-003 (decision_code, LOV-DECISION 'D1 to D9 with sub-decisions'), DF-DEC-011 and DF-DEC-038 (approval_level L1 to L6); Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 rwb-valuation owns the D6 route decision and the route agent output); Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/route (S1) and GET /approvals/{approvalId} (P7); legacy RWB-AD-020 AC1 and AC2
proposed: Fix the names in this contract and record them as assumptions: the four elements are step, autonomyMode, policyVersion and approvalRef on the three reads; the record carries decision_code plus recommendation.autonomyMode and recommendation.policyVersion; the agent output carries a recommendation marker and no applied-outcome element at L1; the rwb-valuation fake stubs POST /api/recovery/valuation/v1/cases/{caseId}/route and the document names the gap in the operation; the four artefacts are named by this story; the sub-decision D6.3 is cited as a value of LOV-DECISION and the range is left to its owner; no requirement ID is cited and the features are traced instead.

title: RWB-E8-004 in rwb-agent: the autonomy level set, the approval reference column, which approval element carries the approved level, the evidence and the breach behind a change, the right the change needs against the legacy permission list, the route, the decision code, the message for a level outside the list and the migration number are not fixed by any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-004); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-020); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.15 and A2.12; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL) and T-A.2 API-P7-008; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 35, 36, 41, 43 and 44; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row E8, P10, FEAT-AGT-15; Ownership Map v1 (agent_* tables and the eleven P10 API rows owner P10; approval and decision_log_entry owner P7; role and permission owner P4)
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC3 to AC10; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 13. Database and migrations; 14. Validation and messages; 15. Screens and states; 18. Traceability
description: The legacy story and its module specification name the behaviour of an approval-gated autonomy change and none of the nine values the rwb-agent slice needs. (1) The autonomy level set is only half defined: LOV-AUTONOMY holds OFF, SHADOW and L1 in TSD P10 v2 T3.2, while legacy RWB-AD-020 AC2 speaks of a committee approval for L2 and no source gives L2, or any level above L1, as a list value or a meaning. (2) The approval reference that legacy RWB-AD-020 AC2 requires the version to show has no column: TSD P10 v2 T3.1 ends agent_policy at DF-AGT-025 approved_by and names no approval element, and no migration number is given for it. (3) Which element of the rwb-decision approval carries the approved autonomy level is not stated, and the two lists collide: the approval carries an approval_level of LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL (L1 to L6, TSD P7 v2 T3.2) and the agent carries an autonomy_mode of LOV-AUTONOMY (OFF, SHADOW, L1), sharing three strings with different meanings. (4) What counts as the measured evidence of a step up and as the breach behind a drop is not given a shape; the sources name the evaluation harness and the drift alert and fix no threshold, sample or condition. (5) The right of the change is a conflict: the legacy permission table gives Platform administration R to six roles, FSD P10 v3 A2.15.3.3 names the risk and model risk officer as the primary user, and TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 gives the load the Rules and parameters right C and the approve the right A, with RW-RISK absent from the legacy six. (6) The gateway-bff route in front of the two admin operations is not named. (7) The decision code of an autonomy change is not named by any source that reaches this story, although the record requires one. (8) The message for a level outside LOV-AUTONOMY is not named: VR-P10-015-1 covers an empty required field with MSG-GEN-001 only. (9) The Flyway number of the approval-reference column is not given. The story keeps the legacy behaviour and settles each value as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-004 sections 1 to 19 (one endpoint row, one screen row, one permission row of six roles, three messages, four test cases); legacy RWB-AD-020 AC2 ('Given a committee approval for L2 / When the new version takes effect / Then the change shows the approval reference in the version'); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.15.3.1 (VR-P10-015-1, BR-P10-015), A2.15.3.2 (agent_policy.autonomy_mode 'Off, shadow or L1'), A2.15.3.3 (roles) and A2.15.4.3 (AC-EXC-P10-015-01 and -02); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025, no approval column), T3.2 (LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, LOV-AGENT), T6.1 (Platform administration R for six roles and CRUD/CRUDA for the two administrator roles) and T-A.1/T-A.2 (API-P10-003 Rules and parameters C, API-P10-004 Rules and parameters A, Idempotency-Key on both); TSD P7 v2 T3.2 LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL (L1 to L6) and T-A.2 API-P7-008 (the approval read); Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41 (rwb-agent owns the policy versions; rwb-decision owns the approvals); slide 43 row 28 (AgentRunCompleted is the only P10 event) and slide 44 (no job for a level change); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row E8, P10, FEAT-AGT-15; Business Requirements Program v4 (no FEAT-AGT-15 match, so no requirement ID)
proposed: Keep the legacy behaviour and settle each open value as an assumption: store only the levels of LOV-AUTONOMY and treat a level above L1 as not storable until the list is extended (ASM-1); take the evidence from agent_policy.evaluation_run_id and the breach from an agent_alert row of type DRIFT (ASM-2, ASM-3); read the approved autonomy level from the approval subject and never from approval_level (ASM-4); add the approval reference as the backward-compatible column approval_ref with its number from the rwb-agent Flyway sequence at build time (ASM-5); keep Platform administration R as the read of SCR-46 and require Rules and parameters C and A for the change, with the RW-RISK right settled by rwb-access (ASM-7); reconcile the level set, the approval element and the right with rwb-access and rwb-decision into the Epic 8 administration scope of RWB-AD-020 before the wave 4 exit.

title: The approval-gated version-change contract of rwb-agent: the field detail of the consumed approval answer, the name and type of the approval reference, the meaning of each 409 and 404, who calls the authorise operation, the record element map of a change with no rule, and the test of a repeated call are not fixed by any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-004); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-020); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2 (API-P10-002 to API-P10-004); TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2 (API-P7-008, ApprovalDetail); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 10, 16, 41 and 43; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11 (the record elements) and slide 12 (ApprovalWorkflow on rwb-decision); Ownership Map v1 (POST /admin/agent-configs and POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve owner P10; approval owner P7)
section: 3. Preconditions; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 11. Data; 12.1 to 12.9; 13. Deliverables; 14. Validation and messages; 19. Out of scope
description: The contract slice rests on six elements that no source states at field level. (1) The answer of API-P7-008 is named ApprovalDetail and described only as 'Read one approval with its routing details for the decision screen'; no property names, types or required flags are given, and none of them says which element carries the approved autonomy level. (2) The approval reference on the configuration version has no agreed name or type: agent_policy stops at DF-AGT-025, and the legacy requirement only says the version shows the approval reference. (3) The error catalogue lists 409 for both operations and 404 for the approve without saying what each means, so a second approval, a four-eyes refusal and an idempotency conflict are indistinguishable in the sources; the four-eyes case is documented for prompt versions in FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03 and not for policies. (4) The Idempotency-Key header is required by TSD P10 v2 T-A.2 but the behaviour of a repeat is stated only by the universal rule R-UNI-40 for events, not for a POST. (5) The authorise operation is the rwb-access contract, and this key has no DP-08 pattern, so no source says whether the service or the gateway-bff route makes the call. (6) The decision record is a fixed thirteen-element shape written in the same transaction, and no source says what each element carries for a change that evaluates no Drools package, where ruleId and ruleVersion cannot be filled. The contract fixes each element and carries these assumptions.
evidence: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.2 API-P7-008 (Purpose: 'Read one approval with its routing details for the decision screen'; Response: ApprovalDetail; Errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 503) and T3.2 LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL and LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.2 API-P10-003 (Errors 401, 403, 409, 422, 503; Idempotency-Key header) and API-P10-004 (Errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 503; Idempotency-Key header) and T3.1 DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03 and A2.15; legacy RWB-AD-020 AC2; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11 (chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash, entry_hash) and slide 12 (ApprovalWorkflow on rwb-decision); Architecture v5 slides 8 and 10 (gateway-bff: one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per service); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-03, DP-13 and DP-19 and §R5.4 (no I dependency outside an ITG story)
proposed: Fix the contract on the agreed readings and carry them as assumptions: the approval reference is the backward-compatible element approval_ref holding the rwb-decision approval id (ASM-5); the approval answer carries the approval id, the status of LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, the decision code and the approved autonomy level of the subject under agreed element names (ASM-11); 409 means the version is not LOADED, or the caller loaded it, and 404 means the version id is unknown, with a repeat under the same Idempotency-Key returning the first answer (ASM-9); the authorise call is the gateway-bff route's and not the service's (ASM-10); the record element map of a change with no rule is agreed with ruleId and ruleVersion empty (ASM-12). Reconcile the approval answer with the rwb-decision owner and the authorise call with the edge owner at the wave 4 contract freeze.

title: Committee review of agent risk in rwb-agent: pack composition, window, export rule, score-fact read path, recorded version, right of the pack read and the Power BI integration point are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-005); WP B-P10-03; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.16 and A2.6; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 34, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 13; Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row E8 P10 FEAT-AGT-16
section: 3. Preconditions; 4. Flow; 7. Acceptance criteria AC3 to AC11; 8. Business rules; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1 to 12.8; 13. Solution plan; 15. Screens and states; 18. Traceability
description: The legacy story names the outcome ('puts agent performance, overrides and incidents in front of the strategy and model committee') and nothing it rests on. Seven values are absent or unresolved. (1) No source states which rows make up the pack: FSD A2.6 fixes the monitor measures (acceptance, override, latency and cost per agent, with the fallback-rate metric and its monthly review) while the legacy Data table names decision_log_entry, v_ace_score and rule_row, which are not the pack. (2) The window of the pack is not stated; FSD A2.6 speaks of a day (2026-12-01) and of a week (the week to 2026-12-14) in different criteria. (3) The export rule is not stated: no source gives the media types, the column order or a file naming rule for a committee pack. (4) The operation and data product by which v_ace_score (DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279) is read from rwb-source-data is named by no source. (5) Legacy AC1 writes the result 'with the rule version', while the target reads no rule_row: no source says which version identifiers the record carries for a committee review that evaluates no Drools package. (6) The right of the pack read is ambiguous: the legacy permission check gives Platform administration R to six roles for GET /admin/agent-runs, TSD T-A.2 gives Platform administration R to API-P10-001 but Rules and parameters R to API-P10-009 (the metrics read of the pack), and the risk and model risk officer that FSD A2.16 names as the primary user is in neither list. (7) FSD A2.16 and A2.6 name Power BI as the integration point while Arch v5 removes the data lake and the Power BI connection (DP-17), so the consumption path of the pack has to be stated by this story. No requirement ID, no pack field list, no threshold and no committee cadence is invented in its place.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-005 (story line, acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2, Data table, Endpoints table GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs with Platform administration R, Permission checks listing RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM and RW-SECADM); FSD P10 v3 A2.16 (metric Agent fallback rate below 10 percent, review monthly; integration points Power BI; prerequisites FEAT-AGT-06) and A2.6 (acceptance, override, latency and cost per agent; AC-ALT-P10-006-01; AC-EXC-P10-006-02); TSD P10 v2 T3.1 agent_run DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060, agent_feedback DF-AGT-097 to DF-AGT-102 with LOV-FEEDBACK, agent_alert DF-AGT-103 to DF-AGT-111 with LOV-AGENT-ALERT, agent_evaluation_run DF-AGT-070 to DF-AGT-085 with failure_counts DF-AGT-083; TSD P10 v2 T6.1 RBAC and T-A.1 API-P10-001 and API-P10-009; T-A.2 errors 401, 403, 503 and 422; Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 43 (EV-28 AgentRunCompleted only), slide 34 note 'No data lake or Power BI connection (INT-19/20 removed)' and slide 44 (no committee job); Ownership Map v1 (agent tables owner P10; GET /admin/agent-runs and GET /admin/agent-metrics owner P10; decision_log_entry owner P7; v_ace_score a P1 data product; rule_row owner P7)
owner_role: Solution architect with the model risk function
proposed: Build the pack from the service's own rows: agent_run for performance and fallbacks, agent_feedback for acceptance and overrides over LOV-FEEDBACK, agent_alert for the incidents over LOV-AGENT-ALERT and agent_evaluation_run for the failure counts, with the window stated as one assumption; read the score facts through the rwb-source-data contract and never from the view; record the policy version in force with the agent, prompt and model versions of the reviewed runs and resolve no Drools package version; serve the pack on the two admin reads of `/api/recovery/agent/v1` through the gateway-bff route and state the CSV and JSON export rule; replace the Power BI integration point with the read operation and the export, because Arch v5 removes the lake; reconcile the pack right with rwb-access.

title: Committee-review read contract of rwb-agent: response element names, export contract, record payload members, errors and the pack right are not published by any source
source: WP B-P10-03 (RWB-P10-E8005-CON); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-005); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T6.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6 and A2.16; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 43; Ownership Map v1; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5
section: 3. Preconditions; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 8. Business rules; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.5 and 12.8; 13. Solution plan
description: The contract slice has to fix shapes that no source publishes. (1) TSD T-A.2 gives the two reads a purpose, a query and a response type name (AgentRun[] for API-P10-001, AgentMetric[] for API-P10-009) and no element list, so the pack resources are a backward-compatible extension whose member names this story fixes. (2) The export is not a contract in any source: the CSV and JSON media types, the column order, the header row and the fact that an export carries the same rows as the read are all unstated. (3) The decision record of a committee outcome is written through the P7 library and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and no source lists the members that a committee review contributes to the record shape. (4) The errors of the two reads come from T-A.2 (401, 403, 503 for the runs read; 401, 403, 422, 503 for the metrics read) but no source states the 422 condition of the metrics read or the problem response of a forbidden export. (5) The rights are split: the legacy story gives Platform administration R to six roles, T-A.2 gives Platform administration R to API-P10-001 and Rules and parameters R to API-P10-009, and the risk and model risk officer is in no list. (6) No fixture list exists for the two fakes of the slice. Nothing is invented as a business value: every open element is carried as a member name with its type taken from the TSD column that owns it, and the values stay rows.
evidence: TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 API-P10-001 (GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs, Platform administration R, first in E1) and API-P10-009 (GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-metrics, Rules and parameters R, first in E2); T-A.2 purpose and response types AgentRun[] and AgentMetric[], request queries agent, from, to and agent, segment, version, from, to, errors 401, 403, 503 and 422; T3.1 field lists of agent_run (DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060), agent_feedback (DF-AGT-097 to DF-AGT-102), agent_alert (DF-AGT-103 to DF-AGT-111), agent_evaluation_run (DF-AGT-070 to DF-AGT-085), agent_policy (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025); T6.1 RBAC matrix; FSD P10 v3 A2.6.3.2 and A2.16.3.2 field catalogs and A2.16.4.3 AC-EXC-P10-016-01 and AC-EXC-P10-016-02; Architecture v5 slide 42 row 08 (DecisionRecorded, rwb.decision-record.v1, all 19 producers); Ownership Map v1 (both operations owner P10; decision_log_entry owner P7; v_ace_score a P1 data product)
owner_role: Solution architect with the tech lead of rwb-agent
proposed: Publish the two read shapes as AgentRunsPack and AgentMetricsPack resources whose members are named after the TSD columns they carry, mark every element that T-A.2 leaves open as an additive extension, fix the CSV and JSON export rule in the same document, declare the committee-outcome members of the P7 record as an additive member set, take the errors and the two rights from T-A.2 with the 422 condition stated by this story, and write the fixtures of the two fakes in the contract tests.
